metaData.originalTitle: 火山引擎 AI 搜索千万级 Agent 架构演进与实践：从 ReAct 三节点到 Unified Policy
metaData.title: Volcengine AI Search 10-Million-Level Agent Architecture Evolution and Practice: From ReAct Three-Node to Unified Policy
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This article details how the Volcengine AI Search team evolved the standard ReAct architecture into a Unified Policy Agent architecture, achieving a 30% reduction in TTFT and improved recommendation quality through Workflow and Agent stratification, and unified control/behavior/state.
metaData.summary: The article deeply analyzes the three major engineering sins of the standard ReAct architecture in enterprise-level AI search scenarios: extremely high latency, context oscillation, and broken control flow. Combining industry consensus, it proposes principles such as strict stratification of Workflow and Agent, everything as a Tool, and context independence. Based on this, the Volcengine AI Search team designed the Workflow + Unified Policy Agent (UP-ReAct) architecture, delegating deterministic processes to Workflow and dynamic decisions to Unified Policy, abstracting all behaviors as Tools, and managing state uniformly via Context Manager. In real e-commerce evaluations, this architecture reduced TTFT from 14.045s to 9.8s (a 30.22% decrease), improved recommendation accuracy by 3.76%, and enhanced conversational experience by 14.78%, breaking the conventional perception that speed and quality are mutually exclusive. The article emphasizes that system complexity should be properly managed through boundary划分, rather than stuffed into the model.

mainPoints.point: The standard ReAct three-node architecture has three major sins in high-concurrency industrial scenarios: high latency, context oscillation, and broken control flow.
mainPoints.explanation: The three nodes require three independent decision flows per call, leading to a sharp deterioration in TTFT; state repetition between nodes causes attention dilution; new tools cannot be naturally integrated, forcing engineers to hard-code If-Else, degrading the system.

mainPoints.point: Industry consensus shifts towards System Engineering: Workflow and Agent stratification, everything as a Tool, context independence, and production-level Eval.
mainPoints.explanation: Predefined paths and hard rules are delegated to Workflow, while Agents only handle dynamic strategy decisions; tools act as strong contracts determining the system's lower bound; context management is independent as a module; the system is measured by multi-dimensional metrics rather than subjective feelings.

mainPoints.point: The Unified Policy Agent solves the pain points of ReAct through unified control, unified behavior, and unified state.
mainPoints.explanation: Thought/Action/Iteration are merged into a single Policy node, completing planning, action selection, and termination determination in a single forward pass; all behaviors are encapsulated as Tools (including exit, deep thinking, etc.); Context Manager manages context via budget windows, semantic compression, and tiered eviction, reducing interference.

mainPoints.point: The new architecture achieves a dual improvement in speed and quality, with TTFT decreasing by 30% while recommendation and conversational quality significantly increase.
mainPoints.explanation: By eliminating redundant nodes and denoising the context, the model's attention is focused on the core objective, reducing the decision distortion rate and breaking the conventional law that speed and quality are mutually exclusive.

keyQuotes: Don't use LLMs for simple switch-cases.
Less talk about tricky Prompts, more talk about solid System Engineering.
The model itself hasn't gotten smarter; we just stopped interfering with it with garbage information.
Respect engineering principles and manage complexity well.
Let large models step down from the pedestal, get into the assembly line, and become extremely robust, stable, and fast industrial-grade productivity engines.

relatedArticles.title: Understanding Harness Engineering: Finding the Shell That Keeps AI from Going Rogue—Insights from 14 Engineering Articles | Hao's Trend Talk
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of "Harness Engineering," a core technology in the AI Agent field. It reveals how to compensate for model shortcomings through a three-layer management architecture and proposes the logic of "Compensation Surface Migration" that evolves with model capabilities.

relatedArticles.title: AI R&D Automation: Wiki Knowledge Base + Skill Pack
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details how to build a continuously growing team knowledge base and a supporting expert skill pack based on the LLM-Wiki model and the Obsidian platform to achieve AI-driven R&D automation.

relatedArticles.title: Understanding Hermes in One Article: How the New Top-Tier Agent Self-Evolves from Experience
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of the core innovation of the Hermes Agent—the Skills closed-loop system—detailing its complete implementation mechanism, from experience extraction and knowledge storage to intelligent retrieval and self-improvement, along with its engineering trade-offs and security considerations.

relatedArticles.title: Coze 2.5: Unveiling a New Agent World!
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: ByteDance has launched Coze 2.5, building an Agent ecosystem with independent identity and execution capabilities through cloud phone/PC hardware foundations, Coze CLI programming tools, and a long-term memory architecture.

relatedArticles.title: Douyin Dynamic Experience Optimization: Practices and Reflections
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details Douyin's self-developed dynamic performance framework DDPF, systematically explaining how on-device intelligence and dynamic scheduling technologies address performance optimization challenges in complex business scenarios, covering framework design, perception and decision-making, and virtual machine tuning.

relatedArticles.title: Coze 3.0 Officially Launched: A New Generation AI Team Starts with Coze
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Coze 3.0 is officially launched, upgrading Agent from a single-point tool to a collaborative AI team through project spaces, multi-device collaboration, and a skill store, ushering in a new way of human-Agent collaboration.

relatedArticles.title: A Game Within a Game! Equipping Agents with OpenViking, They Actually Learned to 'Hold Grudges' and 'Disguise'?
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article introduces ByteDance's open-source OpenViking context management framework and its companion VikingBot, vividly demonstrating through a multi-agent Werewolf game demo how to provide Agents with long-term, traceable collective memory, enabling them to learn across games, form strategies, and simulate complex social behaviors.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Is Not the Goal, Knowledge Is the Moat — Knowledge Accumulation Practices of an AI Engineering Delivery Team
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on the engineering delivery practices of an AI Team, this article proposes that knowledge accumulation is more important than workflow orchestration, and systematically introduces a complete methodology encompassing a five-layer knowledge storage architecture, a three-level maturity system, and how workflows serve knowledge accumulation.

relatedArticles.title: Making Douyin Smooth on Old Phones: The Three Things We Got Right
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: ByteDance shares deep low-level optimization practices for old Android devices across three dimensions: memory (ART heap expansion), FD (breaking the 1024 limit), and threading (M:N user-mode threads).

relatedArticles.title: Investing 10,000 RMB in AI: A Year of Tools, Practices, and Reflections
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: A systematic summary of a veteran developer's practical experience in the AI wave, covering everything from MAC toolchain optimization and Harness Engineering architectural constraints to building an Agent-driven automated learning loop.
